title: Palpation of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Pulses, Landmarks and the Ottawa Rules

hook.en: A few seconds of correct palpation can decide whether an injured ankle needs an X-ray — and a pulse can reveal an artery problem. Learn the landmarks, the pulses and the Ottawa rules.
hook.ur: Sahi palpation ke chand second tay kar sakte hain ke zakhmi ankle ko X-ray chahiye — aur ek pulse artery ka masla dikha sakti hai. Landmarks, pulses aur Ottawa rules seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll palpate the ASIS, greater trochanter, ischial tuberosity, patella, tibial tuberosity, fibular head, malleoli and the main leg pulses, and apply the Ottawa ankle and foot rules.
goal.ur: End tak aap ASIS, greater trochanter, ischial tuberosity, patella, tibial tuberosity, fibular head, malleoli aur leg ki main pulses palpate karenge, aur Ottawa ankle aur foot rules lagayenge.

text.en: Lower-limb landmarks form a map from the pelvis to the toes: **ASIS** (front of the pelvis, level in a normal pelvis), **greater trochanter** (the broad bony prominence on the outside of the hip, about a hand-width below the iliac crest), **ischial tuberosity** (the bone you sit on), **patella**, **tibial tuberosity** (the bump on the shin), **fibular head** (the knob below and behind the outside of the knee, with the common fibular nerve winding round just below), and the **medial and lateral malleoli**. The lateral malleolus extends lower than the medial one.
text.ur: Lower-limb landmarks pelvis se toes tak naqsha banate hain: **ASIS** (pelvis ka samna hissa, normal pelvis mein level), **greater trochanter** (hip ke bahar chauri bony prominence, iliac crest se takriban ek haath ki chorai neeche), **ischial tuberosity** (jis haddi par hum baithte hain), **patella**, **tibial tuberosity** (shin ka bump), **fibular head** (knee ke bahar neeche aur peechay knob, jis ke bilkul neeche common fibular nerve lipti hoti hai) aur **medial aur lateral malleoli**. Lateral malleolus medial se neeche tak jata hai.

text.en: Think of the leg as a road with milestones: ASIS, trochanter, patella, tibial tuberosity, malleoli. When something is injured, you check each milestone in order, because an injury often shows itself as tenderness at one specific milestone — that is why the Ottawa rules work.
text.ur: Taang ko mile ke patharon wali sarak samjhein: ASIS, trochanter, patella, tibial tuberosity, malleoli. Chot lagne par aap har mile ka pathar tarteeb se check karte hain, kyunke chot aksar ek khaas pathar par tenderness ke taur par nazar aati hai — isi liye Ottawa rules kaam karte hain.

intro.en: Follow the iliac crest forward until it ends in a prominent bump at the front. In a normal pelvis the two ASISs are **level**; a difference suggests pelvic tilt or a leg-length difference. The ASIS is the origin of sartorius and the inguinal ligament attaches nearby.
intro.ur: Iliac crest ko aage ki taraf follow karein jab tak woh aage numaya bump par khatam na ho. Normal pelvis mein dono ASIS **level** hote hain; farq pelvic tilt ya leg-length farq batata hai. ASIS sartorius ka origin hai aur inguinal ligament qareeb judta hai.

intro.en: Halfway between the ASIS and the pubic symphysis, press firmly with two fingers and count for 15 seconds. Absent or weak suggests arterial occlusion. The relation is **NAVY**: from the outside in, Nerve, Artery, Vein.
intro.ur: ASIS aur pubic symphysis ke beech mein do fingers se zor se dabayein aur 15 seconds ginein. Gayab ya kamzor arterial occlusion batati hai. Tarteeb **NAVY** hai: bahar se andar Nerve, Artery, Vein.

intro.en: On the top of the foot, lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon, press lightly with two fingertips. It is **absent in about 10% of healthy people**, so always check the posterior tibial pulse (behind the medial malleolus) as well before calling the foot pulseless.
intro.ur: Foot ke top par, extensor hallucis longus tendon ke bahar, do fingertips se halka dabayein. Yeh **takriban 10 % healthy logon mein gayab** hoti hai, is liye foot ko pulseless kehne se pehle posterior tibial pulse (medial malleolus ke peechay) bhi check karein.

question.en: The dorsalis pedis pulse is absent in an otherwise healthy young runner. What should you do before concluding the foot has no pulse?
question.ur: Healthy jawan runner mein dorsalis pedis pulse gayab hai. Foot ko bina pulse kehne se pehle kya karein?

text.en: Check the posterior tibial pulse and the foot's colour, temperature and capillary refill
text.ur: Posterior tibial pulse aur foot ka rang, temperature aur capillary refill check karein

feedback.en: Yes — the dorsalis pedis is congenitally absent in about 1 in 10 people. Look at the whole picture.
feedback.ur: Haan — dorsalis pedis takriban 10 mein se 1 mein paidaishi taur par gayab hoti hai. Poori tasveer dekhein.

text.en: Refer urgently for acute limb ischaemia
text.ur: Acute limb ischaemia ke liye foran refer karein

feedback.en: Not without other signs (cold, pale, painful limb).
feedback.ur: Doosre signs (thandi, peeli, dardnak taang) ke bagair nahi.

text.en: Assume it is normal and move on
text.ur: Normal samajh kar aage barh jayein

feedback.en: You should still check the other pulse and the signs of perfusion.
feedback.ur: Phir bhi doosri pulse aur perfusion ke signs check karein.

title.en: Ottawa ankle and foot rules (after acute injury)
title.ur: Ottawa ankle aur foot rules (acute chot ke baad)

rows.en: Bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus (the distal 6 cm), or unable to bear weight for 4 steps both immediately and in the clinic
rows.ur: Dono malleoli ke peechle kinare ya nok par (distal 6 cm) bony tenderness, ya foran aur clinic mein 4 qadam wazan na utha sakna

rows.en: Press the back edge and tip of the medial and lateral malleolus along the bone
rows.ur: Medial aur lateral malleolus ke peechle kinare aur nok ko haddi ke saath dabayein

rows.en: Bone tenderness at the base of the 5th metatarsal or the navicular, or unable to bear weight for 4 steps
rows.ur: 5th metatarsal ke base ya navicular par bony tenderness, ya 4 qadam wazan na utha sakna

rows.en: Press the base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular tuberosity
rows.ur: 5th metatarsal ka base aur navicular tuberosity dabayein

rows.en: Age 55 or over, isolated tenderness of the patella, tenderness of the fibular head, cannot flex to 90°, or cannot bear weight for 4 steps
rows.ur: Umar 55 ya zyada, sirf patella par tenderness, fibular head par tenderness, 90° tak flex na kar sakna, ya 4 qadam wazan na utha sakna

rows.en: Palpate the patella and fibular head, then test flexion and weight bearing
rows.ur: Patella aur fibular head palpate karein, phir flexion aur weight bearing test karein

text.en: **Skipping the rules or applying them to the wrong patient.** The Ottawa rules are for **acute injuries** in adults (and children over 5 for the ankle, with adaptations); they do not apply to patients who are intoxicated, have reduced sensation, a head injury or multiple injuries, are pregnant or have a diffuse, chronic problem. They are extremely **sensitive (about 98% for fractures)**, so a negative result lets you avoid an X-ray, while a positive one is not proof of a fracture. Never use palpation alone to rule out a fracture in a patient who cannot walk.
text.ur: **Rules chhor dena ya ghalat mareez par lagana.** Ottawa rules adults ki **acute chot** ke liye hain (aur ankle ke liye 5 saal se bade bachon mein tarmeem ke saath); yeh nashay mein, sensation kam, sir ki chot ya kayi chot, hamal wale ya phaile hue, purane masle wale mareezon par laagu nahi. Yeh bohat **sensitive (fractures ke liye takriban 98 %)** hain, is liye negative result X-ray se bacha deta hai, jabke positive result fracture ka saboot nahi. Jo patient chal nahi sakta us mein sirf palpation se fracture rule out kabhi na karein.

question.en: A patient with an ankle sprain has no tenderness over the malleoli or the 5th metatarsal base and walks four steps. What do the Ottawa rules say?
question.ur: Ankle sprain ke patient ko malleoli ya 5th metatarsal base par tenderness nahi aur woh chaar qadam chalta hai. Ottawa rules kya kehte hain?

text.en: An X-ray is not needed (fracture is very unlikely)
text.ur: X-ray ki zaroorat nahi (fracture bohat kam mumkin)

feedback.en: Yes — the rules are highly sensitive, so a negative result safely avoids unnecessary imaging.
feedback.ur: Haan — rules bohat sensitive hain, is liye negative result mehfooz tareeqay se be-zaroorat imaging bachata hai.

text.ur: Har sprain wale ankle ka X-ray karein

feedback.en: That is the unnecessary imaging the rules prevent.
feedback.ur: Yehi be-zaroorat imaging hai jo rules rokte hain.

feedback.en: MRI is not part of this decision.
feedback.ur: MRI is faislay ka hissa nahi.

text.en: **Palpate in a fixed order after injury.** Start away from the pain, then move toward it: the fibular head and neck (the proximal fibula can fracture with an ankle injury), the lateral malleolus (the ATFL lies just in front of it: the commonest ankle sprain), the medial malleolus and deltoid ligament, the base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular. Record the findings against the landmarks and re-palpate at each visit; repeat the Ottawa rules if the pain or weight-bearing changes.
text.ur: **Chot ke baad tay tarteeb se palpate karein.** Dard se door se shuru kar ke us ki taraf barhein: fibular head aur neck (ankle ki chot mein proximal fibula tut sakti hai), lateral malleolus (ATFL iske bilkul samne hota hai: ankle sprain ki sab se aam jagah), medial malleolus aur deltoid ligament, 5th metatarsal ka base aur navicular. Findings ko landmarks ke saath likhein aur har visit par dobara palpate karein; dard ya weight-bearing badle to Ottawa rules dohrayein.

text.en: The Ottawa ankle rules have been validated in many studies and a meta-analysis: sensitivity is about **96–99%** for clinically significant fractures, with specificity around 30–40%. Using them safely reduces ankle X-rays by roughly a third without missing important fractures. The Ottawa knee rule has a similarly high sensitivity (about 98%) and lowers radiography use by about a quarter.
text.ur: Ottawa ankle rules ki kayi studies aur ek meta-analysis mein tasdeeq hui hai: clinically ahem fractures ke liye sensitivity takriban **96–99 %** aur specificity takriban 30–40 % hai. Inhein mehfooz tareeqay se use karne se ahem fractures chhode bagair ankle X-rays takriban ek tihai kam ho jate hain. Ottawa knee rule ki sensitivity bhi isi tarah zyada (takriban 98 %) hai aur radiography ka istemal takriban ek chauthai kam karta hai.

question.en: Why is a high sensitivity more important than high specificity for a rule meant to avoid missing fractures?
question.ur: Aise rule ke liye jo fractures chhootne se bachaye, zyada sensitivity zyada specificity se ahem kyun hai?

answer.en: Because the cost of a missed fracture (untreated, poor healing, long-term disability) is far greater than the cost of an extra X-ray. A highly sensitive rule rarely gives a false negative, so when it is negative you can safely stop; some positives will turn out to be normal, and that is acceptable.
answer.ur: Kyunke chhooti hui fracture ki qeemat (be-ilaaj, kharab healing, lambi disability) ek extra X-ray ki qeemat se kahin zyada hai. Zyada sensitive rule shayad hi false negative deta hai, is liye negative aaye to aap mehfooz tareeqay se ruk sakte hain; kuch positives normal nikalengay aur yeh qabil-e-qabool hai.

question.en: Which landmark is checked for the foot series in the Ottawa rules?
question.ur: Ottawa rules ki foot series mein kaun sa landmark check hota hai?

text.en: The base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular

feedback.en: Yes — bone tenderness at these two sites calls for a foot X-ray.
feedback.ur: Haan — in do jagahon par bony tenderness foot X-ray ki mutalibah karti hai.

feedback.en: That is not an Ottawa foot landmark.
That is not part of the foot series.
feedback.ur: Yeh foot series ka hissa nahi.

text.en: **Refer urgently** for a cold, pale, pulseless foot (acute arterial occlusion), a swollen, tense calf with severe pain (compartment syndrome), a hot swollen joint with fever, an inability to bear any weight, deformity, or signs of fracture or dislocation. Do not test weight-bearing or stress a limb with obvious deformity.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** thanda, peela, bina pulse foot (acute arterial occlusion), sooji, tight calf shadeed dard ke saath (compartment syndrome), garam sooja joint bukhar ke saath, bilkul wazan na utha sakna, deformity, ya fracture ya dislocation ke signs. Wazan ya stress us limb par na daalein jis mein saaf deformity ho.

summary.en: Landmarks from the ASIS to the malleoli map the leg; the ASISs should be level and the lateral malleolus is lower than the medial.
summary.ur: ASIS se malleoli tak landmarks taang ka naqsha banate hain; ASIS level hone chahiye aur lateral malleolus medial se neeche hota hai.

summary.en: Check pulses (femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial) in context; the dorsalis pedis is absent in about 10% of healthy people.
summary.ur: Pulses (femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial) ko context mein check karein; dorsalis pedis takriban 10 % healthy logon mein gayab hoti hai.

summary.en: The Ottawa ankle and foot rules (malleolar and 5th metatarsal/navicular bone tenderness, 4 steps) are highly sensitive and avoid unnecessary X-rays.
summary.ur: Ottawa ankle aur foot rules (malleolar aur 5th metatarsal/navicular bony tenderness, 4 qadam) bohat sensitive hain aur be-zaroorat X-rays se bachate hain.

front.en: What are the Ottawa ankle rule triggers for X-ray?
front.ur: X-ray ke liye Ottawa ankle rule ke triggers?

back.en: Bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus (distal 6 cm), or inability to bear weight for 4 steps.
back.ur: Dono malleoli ke peechle kinare ya nok par (distal 6 cm) bony tenderness, ya 4 qadam wazan na utha sakna.

front.en: What are the foot series landmarks?

back.en: The base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular.

front.en: How common is an absent dorsalis pedis pulse?
front.ur: Dorsalis pedis pulse ka gayab hona kitna aam hai?

back.en: About 10% of healthy people; check the posterior tibial pulse too.
back.ur: Takriban 10 % healthy log; posterior tibial pulse bhi check karein.

front.en: Why is the fibular head important to palpate?
front.ur: Fibular head palpate karna kyun ahem hai?

back.en: It is a landmark for the knee Ottawa rule and the common fibular nerve winds just below it.
back.ur: Yeh knee Ottawa rule ka landmark hai aur common fibular nerve iske bilkul neeche lipti hai.
